approved: Customs and Other Legislation Amendment (Australian Border Force) Bill 2015
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would abolish the Australian Customs and Border Protection Service and create the Australian Border Force within the Department of Immigration and Border Protection from 1 July 2015.
It repeals the Customs Administration Act 1985, transfers customs powers to the Comptroller-General of Customs, and extends the integrity agency ACLEI's oversight to the new department.

The bill also lets the ABF Commissioner, after consulting the Secretary and the Director-General of Security and with the Employment Minister's agreement, declare that parts of the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 do not apply or apply with changes for ABF workers.
Repeals the Customs Administration Act 1985 and abolishes the statutory office of the CEO of Customs.
Confer on the Comptroller-General of Customs all powers and functions currently held by the CEO under the Customs Act and other Commonwealth Acts.
Extend the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity's jurisdiction to cover the whole integrated Department.
Update terminology in the Customs Act and other Acts to remove references to the abolished ACBPS.
Amend the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 to allow the ABF Commissioner to declare that certain provisions do not apply or apply with modifications for ABF workers.
The Australian Border Force, Immigration and Border Protection workers, the Department of Immigration and Border Protection, and the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity.

Introduced consequential legislation to complete the Australian Border Force integration, citing an Australian Crime Commission estimate that organised crime costs Australia $15 billion annually, extending Law Enforcement Integrity Commissioner oversight to the whole department from 1 July 2015, and allowing resignations to be deferred up to 90 days during misconduct investigations.

Labor supported the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 and related legislation, arguing it fulfills a former Labor government commitment to create a single integrated border entity with no greater powers than existing agencies, and includes integrity measures such as drug testing and serious misconduct provisions.

The speaker supported the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 and related legislation, arguing they establish the Australian Border Force Commissioner and a single integrated border entity with integrity provisions including drug/alcohol testing, serious misconduct declarations, and mandatory reporting, while acknowledging border workers' dedication.

The speaker endorsed the Australian Border Force Bill 2015, supporting the coalition's national security policies including citizenship revocation for dual nationals involved in terrorism, and argued the bill would create an integrated border force to handle rising cargo and passenger volumes, with projected savings of $180 million over forward estimates and $100 million annually thereafter.

The speaker supported the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 and its cognate bill, arguing that increased border interactions—44.17% more passenger/crew, 83.59% more air cargo, and 40.6% more sea cargo over the past decade—necessitated the creation of a single integrated Australian Border Force within the Department of Immigration and Border Protection from 1 July. He also criticised the previous government’s border policy, citing 51,798 illegal arrivals and a cost of $11.5 billion, and praised Operation Sovereign Borders.

The speaker argued that the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 and related legislation will improve border security by merging customs and immigration functions under a single commissioner, with projected savings of $180 million over the forward estimates. He contrasted this with the previous Labor government’s border record, citing an $11 billion budget blowout, 50,000 maritime arrivals, over 1,000 drownings at sea, and low cargo examination rates.

The speaker argued for the establishment of the Australian Border Force through the 2015 bills, citing the government's success in stopping illegal boat arrivals (51,000 under Labor, including 8,400 children, with 1,200 lives lost at sea) and getting children out of detention, while also outlining new powers for the Commissioner, drug testing, and misconduct provisions.

The speaker argued that the Customs and Other Legislation Amendment (Australian Border Force) Bill 2015 should be passed to integrate the Department of Immigration and Border Protection with the Australian Customs and Border Protection Service, creating the Australian Border Force by 1 July 2015. The bill is expected to generate $180 million in operating efficiencies and $100 million in annual savings, while strengthening border security against drug smuggling, visa non-compliance, and organised crime.

The speaker argued in favour of the Australian Border Force Bill 2015, which creates a single front-line border enforcement agency combining customs and immigration officers to manage projected increases in travellers and goods. They cited expected efficiencies of $180 million over forward estimates and contrasted the Coalition's border policies with Labor's record of 800 boats and up to 2,000 children in detention.

The speaker supported the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 and related legislation, arguing they would strengthen border protection, save $100 million, and build on Operation Sovereign Borders' success in stopping boat arrivals. They credited the coalition with ending Labor-era detention centre strain in Solomon, citing 800 boats and over 50,000 arrivals, and thanked Ministers Peter Dutton and Scott Morrison.

The speaker supported the Australia Border Force Bill 2015 and the Customs and Other Legislation Amendment (Australian Border Force) Bill 2015, arguing the government fulfilled its election commitment to stop boat arrivals. They cited over 240 days without illegal boat arrivals, one boat in the past year compared to 302 in 2013, and projected $180 million in efficiencies from consolidating immigration and customs into the Australian Border Force.

The speaker argued in support of the Australian Border Force Bill 2015, criticising previous Labor government cuts to border protection agencies that reduced air cargo screening from 60% to 10% and enabled the illegal importation of 220 Glock pistols, with 106 still unaccounted for. The bill establishes the statutory office of the Australian Border Force Commissioner to command a new front-line operational border control entity within the Department of Immigration and Border Protection.

The speaker argued that the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 and the Customs and Other Legislation Amendment (Australian Border Force) Bill 2015 establish the Australian Border Force Commissioner, integrate the Department of Immigration and the Australian Customs and Border Protection Service, and strengthen border integrity and law enforcement, with thanks to Mike Pezzullo and Roman Quaedvlieg.
